key_insight: Combining a retrieval-based library of motion snippets with diffusion-model noise optimization lets a generator satisfy extremely strict spatiotemporal constraints (e.g., obstacle avoidance, exact step counts) in a zero-shot setting.
problem_solved: Existing motion generators struggle with highly-constrained tasks—such as navigating severe spatial obstacles or meeting a specified number of steps—when constraints are unseen at training time; this work enables reliable zero-shot compliance with such challenging spatiotemporal requirements.
method: Retrieve relevant motion snippets from a database to provide strong, context-aware priors for constrained generation.
Run a diffusion-based motion generator whose noise is optimized (guided) at generation time so the sampled trajectory satisfies the user-specified zero-shot goal function.
Combine retrieval priors and constraint-aware noise optimization during denoising to produce plausible, constraint-compliant motions without task-specific retraining.
impact: Enables practical, controllable character animation and virtual-agent behavior that meet precise, previously unseen constraints—reducing manual effort and expanding the range of tasks solvable by generative motion models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing retrieval → diffusion model → noise optimization → constraint-evaluated motion output
Before/after motion sequences illustrating failure of a baseline and success of retrieval-guided diffusion (e.g., navigating an obstacle course or exact-step gait)
Bar/line chart comparing constraint satisfaction rates and motion plausibility across baselines and the proposed method

paper_title: Towards Highly-Constrained Human Motion Generation with Retrieval-Guided Diffusion Noise Optimization
paper_authors: Hanchao Liu, Fang-Lue Zhang, Shining Zhang, Tai-Jiang Mu, Shi-Min Hu
